SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r4.claim: Knowledge is central: God has comprehensive knowledge, angels know only what God teaches them, and Adam is taught what enables him to fulfill the vicegerency.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r4.anchor: إثبات العلم الشامل لله. 2- نفي العلم عن الملائكة إلا ما عَلَّمهم إياه ربُّ العزة

ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r21.claim: The angels glorify God, say they know only what He taught them, and affirm that He is all-knowing and wise.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#5/r21.anchor: Sübhâneke, en yüksek tesbih ve tenzih sana yâ Rab! Senin bize bildirdiğinden başka bizim hiçbir ilmimiz yoktur.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r1.claim: ‘Subhan’ is a proper name for glorification, while ‘Subhanaka’ commonly prefaces repentance.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r1.anchor: “Sübhân”, tesbîhin bir ism-i ‘alemidir. “Sübhâneke” de ekseriya tevbe mukaddimesi olur.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r2.claim: If angels knew no names, would they lack speech entirely and how could they speak? If they only lacked new names, that alone would not prove they were unfit for succession.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r2.anchor: Melâike hiçbir isim bilmiyorlarsa o zaman sıfat-ı kelâmdan külliyen mahrum bulunuyorlardı demek olur.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r3.claim: If the names mean all names, angels lack speech; if they mean descendants’ names, that need not prevent speech, so another wisdom must explain their lack of fitness.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r3.anchor: eğer esmâ-i zürriyet ise, diğer esmâyı men‘etmeyeceğinden sıfat-ı kelâma mâni‘olmaz

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r4.claim: In either interpretation, God’s communication with angels should be understood as knowledge rather than ordinary speech.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r4.anchor: her iki takdirde melâike ile olan muhâtaba-i ilâhiye sıfat-ı kelâma râci‘olmayıp mânası büsbütün başka olmak ve sıfat-ı ilim ile tevil edilmek

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r5.claim: Angels learn names through Adam’s report; knowledge is direct disclosure of reality, while speech conveys it indirectly through signs or deputies.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r9.claim: God’s first address to angels was direct knowledge of reality without named or representative forms; their dialogue, glorification, and sanctification likewise express direct illumination.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r9.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah ile melâikenin evvelki muhâtabaları hiçbir suver-i ismiye ve niyâbiye karışmayan ve bizzat vech-i hakīkat üzerinde vâki‘olan bir cereyân-ı ilmîdir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r10.claim: Angels may lack knowledge or have deficiencies, but do not err or fall into compounded ignorance; they act on revealed text, while humans infer and analogize.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r10.anchor: meleklerin bilmedikleri ve bildiklerinde noksanları bulunabilirse de hataları, cehl-i mürekkebleri olmaz.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r11.claim: The angels did not explicitly claim fitness for succession; they saw the new matter incompletely yet spoke a partial truth without grasping representation’s deeper nature.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r11.anchor: Bâlâdaki ifadelerinde de sarâhaten liyâkat dava etmemişler ve yeni âgâh oldukları meseleyi nâkıs olarak görebilmişler

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r12.claim: Human susceptibility to error and compounded ignorance is tied to speech’s representative nature, through which Satan can mislead.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r12.anchor: Beşeriyetin hata ve cehl-i mürekkeb kabiliyeti de kendilerindeki kelâm sıfatı

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r13.claim: Speech is essentially ordered to truth, yet incidental effects can make it false; people may identify words with knowledge and truth and mistake concepts for reality.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r13.anchor: Gerçi kelâm esasen ilm-i hakka ve sıdka mevzû‘dur ve onun nâibidir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r14.claim: When representation is treated as original and people stop seeking truth beyond it, human evil begins.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r14.anchor: Haslet-i niyâbet, bir asalet telakkī edilir. Ve o zaman insanlığın bütün şerr ü fesâdı başlar.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r15.claim: God gave Adam both knowledge and speech, taught him the names, and tested his fitness before the angels.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#6/r15.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak fıtrat-ı Âdem’i kendi sıfâtından

ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r8.claim: God tested Adam and the angels together, exposed the angels' inability, proved Adam's fitness in practice, and prepared them to submit to him.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r8.anchor: geçirip melaikeye izhâr-ı acz ve ona bilfiil isbât-ı ehliyet ettirmiş

ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r9.claim: The story clearly and subtly reveals how divine lordship manifests, recalls inward blessings embedded in human nature, and leads into the later direct-address warning.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r9.anchor: rubûbiyyet-i ilâhiyenin tarz-ı tecellîsi büyük bir vuzuh ve pek ince bir üslup ile ifham edilerek

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r7.claim: Taqdīs means purification, as in Bayt al-Maqdis and the holy land; quds can mean a purification vessel and qidās a string of pearls.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r7.anchor: التقديس: التطهير، ومنه بيت المقدس والأرض المقدسة، ومنه القدس: السطل الذي يتطهر به، والقداس: الجمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r8.claim: An unnamed poem uses qidās for a string of pearls, while al-Zamakhsharī derives taqdīs from traveling far through the land.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: من قدس في الأرض إذا ذهب فيها وأبعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r6.claim: Subḥānaka means declaring You transcendent; subḥān is a verbal noun used in place of its source and must be governed by an unspoken verb of the same meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r6.anchor: سبحانك: معناه تنزيهك، وسبحان اسم وضع موضع المصدر، وهو مما ينتصب بإضمار فعل من معناه لا يجوز إظهاره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r7.claim: Subḥān is permanently accusative as a verbal noun and may be annexed or used alone; with tanwīn, an unnamed poem attests the standalone form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r7.anchor: وهو من الأسماء التي لزمت النصب على المصدرية، ويضاف ويفرد، فإذا أفرد كان منونا، نحو قول الشاعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r8.claim: One grammatical view explains tanwīn in the standalone poetic subḥānan as poetic declension; another treats it as an indefinite noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r8.anchor: فقيل: صرفه ضرورة، وقيل: لجعله نكرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r9.claim: In an unnamed poem, subḥān is used without tanwīn as a proper name and is diptote because of properness and the augmented alif-nūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r9.anchor: فخبره ... سبحان من علقمة الفاخر جعله علما فمنعه الصرف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r10.claim: Some grammarians say standalone subḥān is cut off from annexation and regains tanwīn, while the untanwinned form is likened to qabl and baʿd; grammar works reject the first account.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r10.anchor: وزعم بعض النحويين أنه إذا أفرد كان مقطوعا عن الإضافة، فعاد إليه التنوين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r11.claim: Ḥakīm is faʿīl with the sense of mufʿil, from making a thing firm and preventing it from departing from its intended state.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r11.anchor: الحكيم: فعيل بمعنى مفعل، من أحكم الشيء: أتقنه ومنعه من الخروج عما يريده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r1.claim: Abū ʿUthmān al-Maghribī says creatures’ affliction is their pretensions: the angels claimed worship, then were brought to admit ignorance; a similar meaning is related from Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r1.anchor: قال أبو عثمان المغربي: ما بلاء الخلق إلا الدعاوى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r2.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r2.claim: A similar meaning of the statement about creatures’ pretensions is related from Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r2.anchor: وروي معنى هذا الكلام عن جعفر الصادق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r3.claim: In the phrase no knowledge except what You taught us, ما is a relative pronoun, preferably nominative as an appositive; an earlier discussion of the syntax of no doubt has already addressed the related jar construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r3.anchor: وما موصولة يحتمل أن تكون في موضع نصب على الاستثناء، والأولى أن تكون في موضع رفع على البدل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r4.speaker: الزهراوي نقلا عن ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r4.claim: Al-Zahrawī, as quoted by Ibn ʿAṭiyya, parses ما as accusative governed by the verb taught; Abu Hayyan calls this unintelligible because the relative clause cannot govern its antecedent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r4.anchor: وحكى ابن عطية عن الزهراوي: أن موضع ما من قولهم:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r5.claim: He sketches a strained alternative: read the exception as disconnected meaning but and ما as a conditional, so they deny all past knowledge and say they will learn whatever God teaches them in future.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r5.anchor: ويكون هذا أبلغ في ترك الدعوى، إذ محوا أنفسهم من سائر العلوم ونفوا جميعها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r6.claim: That hypothetical reading conflicts with reports that God taught the angels or that they knew from the Preserved Tablet about future corruption; if true, they still treat that specific information as nothing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r6.anchor: وهذا الوجه ينافي ما روي أنه كان أعلمهم تعالى، أو علموا باطلاع من اللوح بأنه سيكون في الأرض من يفسد ويسفك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r7.speaker: من اعتقد أن الملائكة غير معصومين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r7.claim: Those who do not consider angels infallible interpret their admission of no knowledge as repentance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r7.anchor: ومن اعتقد أن الملائكة غير معصومين جعل قولهم، لا علم لنا توبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r8.speaker: من اعتقد بعصمتهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r8.claim: Those who hold angels infallible say they acknowledged inability and submitted to knowing only what God taught, or knew the corruption prediction because God informed them but had not taught the names.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r8.anchor: ومن اعتقد بعصمتهم قال: قالوا ذلك على وجه الاعتراف بالعجز والتسليم بأنهم لا يعلمون إلا ما علموا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r9.claim: After disclaiming knowledge for themselves, the angels affirm God’s perfect knowledge and then wisdom; Adam’s demonstrated learning reveals the wisdom of appointing him vicegerent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p238/r9.anchor: ولما نفوا العلم عن أنفسهم أثبتوه لله تعالى على أكمل أوصافه من المبالغة فيه، ثم أردفوا الوصف بالعلم، الوصف بالحكمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r2.claim: In Arabic, successive quoted statements normally need no conjunction marking sequence because their semantic order is clear; he cites the dialogue about the angels and Adam and many Quranic examples.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r2.anchor: والجملة المفتتحة بالقول إذا كانت مرتبا بعضها على بعض في المعنى، فالأصح في لسان العرب أنها لا يؤتى فيها بحرف ترتب

QASHANI:2:31-32/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:31-32/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:31-32/r5.claim: The angels’ answer testifies by their state to their shortfall from human perfection and their inability to attain its ranks by acquiring knowledge, since their perfections accompany their existence.
QASHANI:2:31-32/r5.anchor: شهادة وجوداتهم بالدلالة وألسنة الحال على قصورهم عن الكمالات الإنسانية وتخلفهم عن شأوها

QASHANI:2:31-32/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:31-32/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:31-32/r6.claim: Their answer declares God free of harmful action and affirms that He alone has absolute knowledge and acts wisely.
QASHANI:2:31-32/r6.anchor: وعلمهم بامتناع ترقيهم إلى مراتبهم بكسب العلوم

QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r14.claim: The angels’ reliance on God purified their state and led them to admit ignorance, disclaiming all knowledge beyond what He gave them.
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r14.anchor: اتكالهم علي زكى أحوالهم فألجأهم إلى الاعتراف بالجهالة حتى يتبرأوا عن المعارف إلا بمقدار ما من به الحق عليهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r14.claim: The angels praised God before excusing themselves, acknowledging they lacked the requested knowledge and that no one may blame Him for testing the unable.
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r14.anchor: قدموا الثناء على ذكر ما اعتذروا به

QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r15.claim: Calling God All-Knowing and Wise affirms that whatever He does is true and right, beyond anyone’s judgment and free of folly or wrong.
QUSHAYRI:v1p35/r15.anchor: إنك أنت العليم الحكيم أي ما تفعله فهو حق صدق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r1.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r1.claim: Al-Baghawi says the angels were ordered to prostrate before Adam's creation was completed, immediately after the spirit was breathed into him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p102/r1.anchor: أن الأمر بالسجود له كان قبل إتمام خلقه وأن السجود كان عقب النفخ , وبه صرح البغوي في تفسيره

DURR-FULL:v1p120/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r12.claim: The angels' glorification exonerates God from anyone else knowing the unseen; their denial of knowledge is limited to what God taught them.
DURR-FULL:v1p120/r12.anchor: {قالوا سبحانك} تنزيها لله من أن يكون يعلم الغيب أحد غيره تبنا إليك {لا علم لنا} تبريا منهم من علم الغيب {إلا ما علمتنا}

DURR-FULL:v1p121/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r3.speaker: قتادة والحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r3.claim: The angels privately claimed superiority in knowledge and honor; after Adam was created, God commanded them to prostrate, demonstrated his precedence by teaching him the names, and they repented when unable to answer.
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r3.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن قالا: لما أخذ الله في خلق آدم همست الملائكة فيما بينها فقالوا: لن يخلق الله خلقا إلا كنا أعلم منه وأكرم عليه منه

DURR-FULL:v1p121/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r5.claim: They explain the angels' challenge as referring to their claim that Adam's descendants would corrupt the earth and shed blood.
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة في قوله {إن كنتم صادقين} قال: إن بني آدم يفسدون في الأرض ويسفكون الدماء

AKHFASH:v1p63/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p63/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p63/r3.claim: The angels then acknowledged that they knew nothing of the unseen, speaking about themselves in a way parallel to God's report of them.
AKHFASH:v1p63/r3.anchor: ونحن نعلم أنه لا علم لنا بالغيب" إخبارا عن أنفسهم بنحو ما خبر الله عنهم.

AKHFASH:v1p63/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p63/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p63/r4.claim: “Subḥānaka” is accusative as a substitute for the verbal expression “nusabbiḥuka,” effectively “we glorify You with glorification”; subḥān is an indeclinable verbal noun.
AKHFASH:v1p63/r4.anchor: وقوله {سبحانك لا علم لنآ} فنصب "سبحانك" لانه أراد "نسبحك" جعله بدلا من اللفظ بالفعل

AKHFASH:v1p63/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p63/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p63/r5.claim: In exegesis subḥān means disavowal and declaring someone free of defect; the cited line uses it as a word of repudiation.
AKHFASH:v1p63/r5.anchor: أقول لما جاءني فخره * سبحان من علقمة الفاخر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r11.claim: Subḥānaka means declaring God transcendent and affirming that no one knows anything of His knowledge except what He teaches; it is accusative as a verbal noun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r11.anchor: وسبحانك معناه: تنزيها لك وتبرئة أن يعلم أحد من علمك إلا ما علمته، وسبحانك نصب على المصدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r12.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r12.claim: Al-Kisāʾī parses subḥānaka as an annexed vocative rather than a verbal noun.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r13.speaker: الزهراوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r13.claim: Al-Zahrawī says mā is accusative as the object of ʿallamtanā, while another parsing makes it nominative as a substitute for the predicate of the acquittal; anta may emphasize innaka’s pronoun or begin a clause with al-ʿalīm as predicate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r13.anchor: موضع ما من قولهم ما علمتنا نصب ب علمتنا، وخبر التبرئة في لنا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r1.speaker: الزهراوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r1.claim: The continuation parses al-ʿalīm as the predicate of anta and the sentence as the predicate of inna, or as a nonparsing separator.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r1.anchor: والعليم خبره، والجملة خبر «إن» ، أو فاصلة لا موضع لها من الإعراب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r2.claim: Al-ʿAlīm means “the Knowing,” with an added sense of abundance and comprehensiveness of what is known in God’s case.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r2.anchor: والعليم معناه: العالم، ويزيد عليه معنى من المبالغة والتكثير من المعلومات في حق الله عز وجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r3.claim: Al-Ḥakīm means “the Ruler,” with an added sense of intensification.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r3.anchor: والحكيم معناه الحاكم، وبينهما مزية المبالغة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r4.claim: Others take al-Ḥakīm to mean “the One who makes things firm”; the cited verse calls al-samīʿ “the One who makes hear.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r4.anchor: وقيل: معناه المحكم كما قال عمرو بن معديكرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r5.claim: The interpretation of ḥakīm as “making firm” belongs to the attributes of action.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r6.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r6.claim: Another group defines al-Ḥakīm as the One who prevents corruption, linking the word to the horse’s bridle and citing Jarīr’s use of aḥkimū for restraining fools.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r6.anchor: الحكيم المانع من الفساد، ومنه حكمة الفرس مانعته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r7.speaker: جرير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r7.claim: Jarīr’s line uses aḥkimū to mean restrain or control, as evidence for this sense of ḥakīm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p122/r7.anchor: أبني حنيفة أحكموا سفهاءكم ... إني أخاف عليكم أن أغضبا

MAJAZ:v1p36/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p36/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p36/r3.claim: Subḥānaka declares God transcendent and disavows the claim.

MAJAZ:v1p36/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p36/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p36/r4.claim: Al-Aʿshā uses subḥān in a line disclaiming and denying ʿAlqama’s boast.
MAJAZ:v1p36/r4.anchor: أقول لما جاءنى فخره ... سبحان من علقمة الفاخر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r25.claim: Al-ʿAlīm is one who knows without being taught.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r25.anchor: العليم : هو العالم من غير تعليم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r26.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r26.claim: Al-Ḥakīm may mean that God makes His acts sound and precise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r26.anchor: وفي ( الحكيم ) ثلاثة أقاويل : أحدها : أنه المحكم لأفعاله

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r27.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r27.claim: Al-Ḥakīm may mean that God prevents corruption, as a bridle restrains a horse from excessive running.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98#2/r27.anchor: والثاني : أنه المانع من الفساد , ومنه سميت حكمة اللجام , لأنها تمنع الفرس من الجري الشديد

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.claim: Eve enters without an account of her origin; although primordial Adam represents all humanity, male and female, the Quran does not explain how this Adam becomes the first couple.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.anchor: the Quran does not explicitly discuss the process by which this primordial Adam is differentiated into the first male and female

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:31-32/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:31-32/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:31-32/r5.claim: The angels' glorification rejects any objection to God's judgment, and they confess they cannot know what He has not taught them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:31-32/r5.anchor: تنزيها لك عن الاعتراض عليك في حكمك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:31-32/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:31-32/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:31-32/r6.claim: The angels acknowledge their inability to know what they were not taught.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:31-32/r6.anchor: اعترفوا بالعجز عن علم ما لم يعلموه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:31-32/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:31-32/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:31-32/r7.claim: Al-ʿAlīm means the All-Knowing, and al-Ḥakīm here means the Judge who rules justly.

STUDYQURAN:2:32/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:32/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:32/r1.claim: The verse shows that angels' knowledge is limited with respect to its universal, comprehensive scope.
STUDYQURAN:2:32/r1.anchor: This verse indicates the limitation of the knowledge of God by angels as far as the universal comprehensive nature of this knowledge is concerned.

TAB-FULL:v1p527/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r1.claim: The angels turn back to God, entrust to Him what they did not know, and disclaim any knowledge except what He taught them.
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r1.anchor: بالأوبة إليه، وتسليم علم ما لم يعلموه له، وتبريهم من أن يعلموا

TAB-FULL:v1p527/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r2.claim: God's disclosure of unseen matters to Muhammad, inaccessible except by revelation, establishes his prophethood before the Jews and shows his message comes from God.
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r2.anchor: احتج فيها لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم على من كان بين ظهرانيه من يهود بني إسرائيل بإطلاعه إياه من علوم الغيب

TAB-FULL:v1p527/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r3.claim: Anyone claiming knowledge of unseen events without transmitted report or proof deserves punishment; this rebukes soothsayers, diviners, fortune tellers, and astrologers.
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r3.anchor: كل مخبر خبرا عما قد كان أو عما هو كائن مما لم يكن ولم يأته به خبر

TAB-FULL:v1p527/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r4.claim: The account recalls God's favors to the ancestors of the People of Scripture to draw them toward guidance and warns that persistent rebellion brings punishment like Iblis received.
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r4.anchor: مستعطفهم بذلك إلى الرشاد، ومستعتبهم به إلى النجاة، وحذرهم بالإصرار والتمادي في البغي

TAB-FULL:v1p528/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p528/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p528/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the angels' words as exalting God as the sole knower of the unseen, repenting, and disclaiming unseen knowledge except what God taught, as He taught Adam.
TAB-FULL:v1p528/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: قالوا: " {سبحانك} [البقرة: 32] تنزيها لله من أن يكون أحد يعلم الغيب غيره

TAB-FULL:v1p528/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p528/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p528/r2.claim: Subḥān is a verbal noun that does not inflect.

TAB-FULL:v1p528/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p528/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p528/r3.claim: The angels mean, 'We glorify and exalt You,' clearing God of any claim that they know anything beyond what He taught.
TAB-FULL:v1p528/r3.anchor: نسبحك تسبيحا، وننزهك تنزيها، ونبرئك من أن نعلم شيئا غير ما علمتنا

TAB-FULL:v1p529/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p529/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p529/r1.claim: God knows all past and future and the unseen without being taught; unlike creatures, He has no need of another to teach Him.
TAB-FULL:v1p529/r1.anchor: العليم من غير تعليم بجميع ما قد كان وما وهو كائن، والعالم للغيوب دون جميع خلقك

TAB-FULL:v1p529/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p529/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p529/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-ʿAlīm as the One perfected in knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v1p529/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {العليم} [البقرة: 32] : الذي قد كمل في علمه؛ و {الحكيم} [البقرة: 32] : الذي قد كمل في حكمه "

TAB-FULL:v1p529/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p529/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p529/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-Ḥakīm as the One perfected in judgment.
TAB-FULL:v1p529/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {العليم} [البقرة: 32] : الذي قد كمل في علمه؛ و {الحكيم} [البقرة: 32] : الذي قد كمل في حكمه "

TAB-FULL:v1p529/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p529/r4.speaker: قيل
TAB-FULL:v1p529/r4.claim: Another reported gloss takes al-Ḥakīm to mean judge or ruler, parallel to al-ʿAlīm meaning knower and al-Khabīr meaning aware.
TAB-FULL:v1p529/r4.anchor: وقد قيل: إن معنى الحكيم: الحاكم، كما أن العليم بمعنى العالم

TABRISI:2:32/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:32/r1.claim: حكمة is the opposite of foolishness; إحكام means precision, and حكيم describes one who prevents corruption.
TABRISI:2:32/r1.anchor: الحكمة نقيض السفه والإحكام الإتقان والحكيم المانع من الفساد

TABRISI:2:32/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:32/r2.claim: The bridle’s حكمة restrains a horse from rushing; Jarīr uses أحكموا to mean “restrain.”
TABRISI:2:32/r2.anchor: ومنه حكمة اللجام لأنها تمنع الفرس من الجري الشديد قال جرير

TABRISI:2:32/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:32/r3.claim: Wisdom brings one to unalloyed truth and honesty; a wise person is characterized by knowledge that prevents ignorance.
TABRISI:2:32/r3.anchor: والحكمة هي التي تقف بك على مر الحق الذي لا يخلطه باطل والصدق

TABRISI:2:32/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r4.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:2:32/r4.claim: Sībawayh parses سبحان as a verbal noun standing in place of تسبيح; it is in the accusative as a cognate verbal noun.
TABRISI:2:32/r4.anchor: سبحانك نصب على المصدر قال سيبويه سبحت الله تسبيحا وسبحانا

TABRISI:2:32/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:32/r5.claim: لنا depends on an omitted element and forms a locative predicate; ما علمتنا is a relative clause whose omitted pronoun is replaced by the nominative phrase لا علم.
TABRISI:2:32/r5.anchor: واللام من قوله لنا يتعلق بمحذوف فيكون جملة ظرفية في موضع رفع بالخبر

TABRISI:2:32/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:32/r6.claim: أنت may be a noninflecting separator, leaving العليم الحكيم as إنّ’s predicate, or may be the subject of a clause that predicates إنّ.
TABRISI:2:32/r6.anchor: أنت يجوز أن يكون فصلا فيكون لا موضع له من الإعراب

TABRISI:2:32/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:32/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses سبحانك as declaring God exalted above anyone else knowing the unseen.
TABRISI:2:32/r7.anchor: تنزيها لك وتعظيما عن أن يعلم الغيب أحد سواك عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:2:32/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r8.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:32/r8.claim: Another gloss is that the angels declare God exalted above being challenged over His judgment.
TABRISI:2:32/r8.anchor: وقيل تنزيها لك عن الاعتراض عليك في حكمك

TABRISI:2:32/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:32/r9.claim: They may have answered reverently, disavowing any attribution of wrongdoing while admitting they did not see the wisdom in God’s acts.
TABRISI:2:32/r9.anchor: وقيل إنهم أرادوا أن يخرجوا الجواب مخرج التعظيم فقالوا تنزيها لك عن فعل قبيح

TABRISI:2:32/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:32/r10.claim: A further reading treats the angels’ words as astonishment at being asked about something they do not know.
TABRISI:2:32/r10.anchor: وقيل إنه على وجه التعجب لسؤالهم عما لا يعلمونه

TABRISI:2:32/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:32/r11.claim: The angels say they know only through God’s teaching, and that these names were not among what He taught them.
TABRISI:2:32/r11.anchor: معناه إنا لا نعلم إلا بتعليمك وليس هذا فيما علمتنا

TABRISI:2:32/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:32/r12.claim: They could have stopped at “we have no knowledge”; adding the exception honors God, acknowledges His teaching, and says all their knowledge comes from Him.
TABRISI:2:32/r12.anchor: ولو أنهم اقتصروا على قولهم لا علم لنا لكان كافيا في الجواب لكن أرادوا أن يضيفوا إلى ذلك التعظيم له

TABRISI:2:32/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:32/r13.claim: God asks about what the angels do not know to establish their dependence on His teaching and raise Adam by showing that he learned what they had not.
TABRISI:2:32/r13.anchor: وإنما سألهم سبحانه عما علم أنهم لا يعلمونه ليقررهم على أنهم لا يعلمون إلا ما علمهم الله

TABRISI:2:32/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:32/r14.claim: العليم means one who knows every knowable; it is an emphatic form of عالم and an essential attribute.
TABRISI:2:32/r14.anchor: أي العالم بجميع المعلومات لأنه من صفات ذاته

TABRISI:2:32/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r15.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:32/r15.claim: The angels affirm that God knows without being taught, whereas they are learners.
TABRISI:2:32/r15.anchor: وقيل إنهم أثبتوا له ما نفوه عن أنفسهم أي أنت العالم من غير تعليم

TABRISI:2:32/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:32/r16.claim: حكيم may mean knowing, an eternal essential attribute; or one who makes acts precise, an active attribute whose acts are all wise and sound.
TABRISI:2:32/r16.anchor: الحكيم } يحتمل أمرين - أحدهما: أنه بمعنى العالم

TABRISI:2:32/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:32/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says العليم is perfect in knowledge and الحكيم perfect in wisdom.
TABRISI:2:32/r17.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال:

TABRISI:2:32/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:32/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:32/r18.claim: All knowledge comes from God: He produces necessary knowledge and establishes the proofs on which inferential knowledge depends.
TABRISI:2:32/r18.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن العلوم كلها من جهته تعالى وإنما كان كذلك لأن العلوم لا تخلو

THALABI:v1p178/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p178/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p178/r4.claim: The angels' declaration exonerates God from objection concerning His knowledge, judgment, and governance.
THALABI:v1p178/r4.anchor: تنزيها لك عن الاعتراض لعلمك في حكمك وتدبيرك

THALABI:v1p178/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p178/r5.speaker: الخليل
THALABI:v1p178/r5.claim: Al-Khalil parses subḥānaka as an accusative verbal noun, meaning we glorify You with glorification.
THALABI:v1p178/r5.anchor: وهو نصب على المصدر، أي نسبح سبحانا في قول الخليل

THALABI:v1p178/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p178/r6.speaker: الكسائي
THALABI:v1p178/r6.claim: Al-Kisa'i says subḥānaka is outside ordinary description.

THALABI:v1p178/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p178/r7.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v1p178/r7.claim: Another parsing takes it as an annexed vocative: O Your Glory.
THALABI:v1p178/r7.anchor: وقيل: على النداء المضاف أي: يا سبحانك

THALABI:v1p178/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p178/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p178/r8.claim: The angels profess that their knowledge is only what God taught them and describe Him as all-knowing of His creation and wise in His command.
THALABI:v1p178/r8.anchor: لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا إنك أنت العليم بخلقك الحكيم في أمرك

THALABI:v1p178/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p178/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p178/r9.claim: One sense of ḥakīm is the one who makes an act exact; the pattern faʿīl can mean the causative doer, as in painful and aching, making the attribute one of action.
THALABI:v1p178/r9.anchor: أحدهما: المحكم للفعل، كقوله: عذاب أليم، وحز وجيع

THALABI:v1p178/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p178/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p178/r10.claim: The other sense is judge and knower, in which case ḥakīm is an attribute of essence; ḥikma originally means restraint, as wisdom prevents falsehood and flaws.
THALABI:v1p178/r10.anchor: والآخر: بمعنى (الحاكم العالم) وحينئذ يكون صفة ذات

THALABI:v1p178/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p178/r11.speaker: جرير
THALABI:v1p178/r11.claim: Jarir's command to the Banu Hanifa to restrain their fools illustrates ḥikma as prevention.
THALABI:v1p178/r11.anchor:
قال جرير:
أبني حنيفة احكموا سفهاءكم …

THALABI:v1p178/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p178/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p178/r12.claim: The verse proves that God may impose an impossible task: He ordered angels to report what they did not know while knowing they could not do it.
THALABI:v1p178/r12.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دليل على جواز تكليف ما لا يطاق حيث أمر الله تعالى الملائكة بإنباء ما لم يعلموا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses Subhanaka as exalting and glorifying God above anyone besides Him knowing the unseen.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: تنزيها لك وتعظيما عن أن يعلم الغيب أحد (¬3) سواك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r2.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r2.claim: Another explanation takes the phrase as declaring God too exalted for anyone to object to His judgment and governance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r2.anchor: وقيل: تنزيها لك عن الاعتراض عليك في حكمك وتدبيرك (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r3.speaker: الخليل والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r3.claim: They parse subhana as an accusative verbal noun standing in place of tasbih, as in the expression Subhan Allah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r3.anchor: وهو منصوب على المصدر عند الخليل والفراء، إذا قلت: (سبحان الله)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r4.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r4.claim: Sibawayh says tasbih and subhan share a meaning: tasbih is the verbal noun, while subhan is a noun that serves in its place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r4.anchor: فالمصدر: تسبيح، وسبحان اسم يقوم مقام المصدر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r5.speaker: أبو الخطاب الكبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r5.claim: Abu al-Khattab explains Subhan Allah as God's freedom from evil, illustrated by al-A'sha's line using subhan in the sense of disavowal.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r5.anchor: وقال أبو الخطاب الكبير (¬1): سبحان الله، كقولك: براءة الله من السوء، ومنه قول الأعشى:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r6.speaker: النضر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r6.claim: Al-Nadr recounts a dream interpreter's gloss of Subhan Allah as speed toward God, drawing on the horse's rapid movement called swimming.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r6.anchor: وقال النضر: رأيت في المنام كأن إنسانا فسر لي سبحان الله، قال: أما ترى الفرس يسبح، يريد السرعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r7.claim: The author refers readers to his earlier explanation of tasbih at the angels' statement in 2:30.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p351/r7.anchor: وقد ذكرنا معنى التسبيح عند قوله: {ونحن نسبح بحمدك} (¬5).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p352/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p352/r1.speaker: المفسرون وأهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p352/r1.claim: The angels admit they cannot know what God has not taught them, acknowledging that all their knowledge comes from Him; saying only We do not know this would omit that praise and recognition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p352/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون وأهل المعاني: هذا اعتراف (عن) (¬6) الملائكة بالعجز عن علم ما لم يعلموه فكأنهم قالوا: لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p352/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p352/r2.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p352/r2.claim: An alternative reads this as a tactful request for knowledge and repentance for their uninformed question about appointing Adam; ignorance of names teaches them their greater ignorance of unseen outcomes and warns against judging themselves obedient.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p352/r2.anchor: وقيل: إنه تلطف في طلب علم ما لم يعلموه، وتوبة عن قولهم: {أتجعل فيها} من غير علم لهم بذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r1.claim: Al-Alim means the One who knows without being taught.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {إنك أنت العليم}. أي العالم غير المعلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r2.claim: Al-Hakim can mean the One who makes things firm and well ordered; morphologically it shifts from mufil to faʿil, as samiʿ can mean one who causes hearing and alim one who causes pain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r2.anchor: ومعنى: (الحكيم) هو المحكم للأشياء (¬6) صرف من (مفعل) إلى (فعيل) كالسميع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r3.claim: The author also allows Hakim to mean ruler or judge, as qadir and alim each have corresponding forms; it can mean the one who knows or judges justly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى: حاكم، كالقدير والقادر، والعليم والعالم، ويكون معناه العالم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r4.speaker: ابن المظفر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r4.claim: Ibn al-Muzaffar says hukm can mean knowledge, as in God's granting judgment to John as a child, and can also mean judging with justice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r4.anchor: قال ابن المظفر (¬2): والحكم: العلم (¬3)، قال الله تعالى: {وآتيناه الحكم صبيا} [مريم: 12].

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r5.speaker: النابغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r5.claim: Al-Nabigha's line uses the root in a sense of judgment, asking for a decision like that of the young woman who observed the doves.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r5.anchor:
قال النابغة:
واحكم كحكم فتاة الحي إذ نظرت ... إلى حمام سراع وارد الثمد (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r6.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r6.claim: Al-Asmaʿi derives governance from restraining a person from injustice and a bridle's ḥikma from restraining an animal; Labid's verse uses ahkim for holding a sword back from the armor's openings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r6.anchor: قال الأصمعي: أصل الحكومة: رد الرجل عن الظلم، ومنه سميت حكمة اللجام، لأنها ترد الدابة، قال (¬1) ومنه قول لبيد:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r7.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r7.claim: Al-Azhari says the Arabic forms ḥakamtu, aḥkamt, and ḥakkamt can mean I restrained or prevented; a judge is so named because he prevents injustice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r7.anchor: قال الأزهري: والعرب تقول: حكمت وأحكمت وحكمت بمعنى: رددت ومنعت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r8.speaker: جرير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r8.claim: Jarir's command ahkimu sufahaakum means restrain your foolish people from causing trouble.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r8.anchor:
وقال جرير:
أبني حنيفة أحكموا سفهاءكم (¬1) يقول: امنعوهم من التعرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r9.speaker: النخعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r9.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi says to govern an orphan as one governs one's child; Abu ʿUbayd explains this as preventing the orphan from corruption, since restraint is the core sense of the verb.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r9.anchor: وروي عن النخعي أنه قال: حكم اليتيم كما تحكم ولدك (¬3). قال أبو عبيد: يقول: امنعه من الفساد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r10.claim: Wisdom is knowledge that prevents ignorance; a judge prevents injustice, and any well-made work is protected from corruption.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p353/r10.anchor: والحكمة: هي العلم الذي يمنع [صاحبه] (¬6) من الجهل، والحاكم الذي يمنع من الجور

BURHAN:v3p247/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p247/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p247/r1.claim: Ordering “the Knowing” before “the Wise” can show that sound judgment follows knowledge; knowledge may also be first because it is an essential attribute.
BURHAN:v3p247/r1.anchor: وتقديم العليم على الحكيم لأن الإتقان ناشىء عن العلم

BURHAN:v3p247/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p247/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p247/r2.claim: In this instance, “the Knowing” may be placed first simply to correspond to the preceding “we have no knowledge.”
BURHAN:v3p247/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون قدم وصف العلم هنا ليتصل بما يناسبه

BURHAN:v4p400/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p400/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p400/r4.claim: Ma is declarative or relative before laysa, lam, or la, and after illa, as in the cited examples.
BURHAN:v4p400/r4.anchor: إذا جاءت قبل ليس أو لم أو لا أو بعد إلا فإنها تكون خبرية

BURHAN:v4p400/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p400/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p400/r5.claim: Ma after a preposition is generally declarative, except after the comparative kaf; after ba it may instead be a verbal noun.
BURHAN:v4p400/r5.anchor: وكذلك إذا جاءت بعد حرف الجر نحو ربما وعما وفيما ونظائرهاإلا بعد كاف التشبيه

ITQAN:v2p476#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p476#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p476#2/r1.claim: Subhan is a verbal noun of glorification, obligatorily accusative and annexed to an explicit or implicit singular; its verb has fallen out of use.
ITQAN:v2p476#2/r1.anchor: مصدر بمعنى التسبيح لازم النصب والإضافة إلى مفرد ظاهر نحو

ITQAN:v2p476#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p476#2/r2.speaker: المفصل
ITQAN:v2p476#2/r2.claim: Al-Mufassal gives the unusual derivation from sabaha, ‘to raise one’s voice’ in supplication and remembrance, citing a line about Taghlib and pilgrims praising God.
ITQAN:v2p476#2/r2.anchor: وفي العجائب للكرماني من الغريب ما ذكره المفصل أنه مصدر سبح إذا رفع صوته بالدعاء والذكر وأنشد

ITQAN:v2p476#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p476#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p476#2/r3.claim: Ibn ‘Abbas explains ‘subhan Allah’ as God’s declaring Himself free of evil.
ITQAN:v2p476#2/r3.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس في قوله ﴿ سبحان الله ﴾ قال تنزيه الله نفسه عن السوء

NAHHAS:v1p210/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p210/r6.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p210/r6.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh parse subḥānaka as an accusative verbal noun conveying “we glorify You with glorification.”
NAHHAS:v1p210/r6.anchor: منصوب على المصدر عند الخليل وسيبويه يؤدي عن معنى نسبحك سبحانك تسبيحا

NAHHAS:v1p210/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p210/r7.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v1p210/r7.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says subḥānaka is accusative because it has no adjective, and also allows it as an annexed vocative.
NAHHAS:v1p210/r7.anchor: وقال الكسائي هو منصوب لأنه لم يوصف قال ويكون منصوبا على أنه نداء مضاف

NAHHAS:v1p210/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p210/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p210/r8.claim: Lā ʿilma lanā follows the same analysis as lā rayba fīhi: lā negates an indefinite noun.
NAHHAS:v1p210/r8.anchor: مثل لا ريب فيه ويجوز لا علم لنا يجعل لا بمعنى ليس

NAHHAS:v1p210/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p210/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p210/r9.claim: Lā may alternatively mean laysa in the phrase “we have no knowledge.”
NAHHAS:v1p210/r9.anchor: يجعل لا بمعنى ليس المعنى ليس

NAHHAS:v1p210/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p210/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p210/r10.claim: Mā is nominative, like the exception in lā ilāha illā Allāh, with the negation’s predicate like a subject’s predicate; accusative is also possible after a complete clause as an ordinary exception.
NAHHAS:v1p210/r10.anchor: ما في موضع رفع كما تقول لا إلاه إلا الله وخبر التبرية كخبر الابتداء

NAHHAS:v1p210/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p210/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p210/r11.claim: An alternative permits accusative mā if the clause is treated as complete before the exception.
NAHHAS:v1p210/r11.anchor: ويجوز النصب إذا تم الكلام على أصل الاستثناء

NAHHAS:v1p210/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p210/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p210/r12.claim: Anta can be accusative as emphasis of the pronoun in inna, or nominative as a subject with al-ʿalīm as predicate, or a syntactic separator; the Kūfans call it ʿimād and make it nominative.
NAHHAS:v1p210/r12.anchor: أنت في موضع نصب توكيدا للكاف وإن شئت كانت رفعا بالابتداء والعليم خبره

SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r1.claim: سبحان is either an اسم مصدر meaning tasbīḥ or a verbal noun because a triliteral verb is attested.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r1.anchor: " سبحان " اسم مصدر وهو التسبيح، وقيل: بل هو مصدر لأنه سمع له فعل ثلاثي

SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r2.claim: سبحان normally remains in construct but may occur alone; when definite it is diptote for proper-name status and extra alif-nūn.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r2.anchor: وهو من الأسماء اللازمة للإضافة وقد يفرد، وإذا أفرد منع الصرف للتعريف وزيادة الألف والنون

SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r3.claim: Poetic سبحان من علقمة الفاخر illustrates standalone use; tanwīn in سبحانه ثم سبحانا is explained as poetic necessity or declension of an indefinite like قبل/بعد, supporting the verbal-noun view; the first view can answer it is an indefinite obligatorily accusative with an unexpressed verb.

SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r4.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī parses سبحانك as vocative يا سبحانك; most grammarians reject this.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r4.anchor: وقد روي عن الكسائي أنه جعله منادى تقديره: يا سبحانك، وأباه الجمهور من النحاة

SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r5.claim: The annexation may be to the object, meaning we glorify You, or to the subject, meaning You are free of evil and transcendent.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r5.anchor: وإضافته [هنا] إلى المفعول لأن المعنى: نسبحك نحن. وقيل: بل إضافته للفاعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r6.claim: The عامل governing سبحان in the accusative is the verb of saying.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32/r6.anchor: والعامل فيه في محل نصب بالقول

SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r1.claim: The construction parallels لا ريب فيه; إلا introduces an exception, and ما is relative with علمتنا as its clause and omitted resumptive if علم means معلوم.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r1.anchor: و " إلا " حرف استثناء، و " ما " موصولة، و " علمتنا " صلتها

SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r2.claim: Alternatively ما is a verbal noun and accusative as exception; it cannot be governed by علم, the noun of لا, since a governing noun would be declinable.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون مصدرية وهي في محل نصب على الاستثناء

SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r3.claim: Another view puts ما in the nominative by position as بدل of the noun of لا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: في محل رفع على البدل من اسم " لا " على الموضع

SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls it بدل of the predicate of لا, analogizing لا إله إلا الله; al-Samīn objects that exception is from the judged subject, not the predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " هو بدل من خبر التبرئة كقولهم

SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r5.speaker: الزهراوي
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r5.claim: Al-Zahrawī is reported to make ما the object of the following علمتنا; al-Samīn says a relative is not governed by its own clause.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r5.anchor: ونقل هو عن الزهراوي أن " ما " منصوبة بعلمتنا بعدها

SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r6.claim: The shaykh offers a remote rescue: disconnected exception meaning لكن, with conditional ما governed by علمتنا in the jussive and omitted response, yielding but what You taught us, we knew.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#2/r6.anchor: إلا أن يتكلف له وجه بعيد، وهو أن يكون استثناء منقطعا بمعنى لكن

SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r1.claim: أنت may be emphatic for the noun of إن and accusative in position.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r1.anchor: أن يكون تأكيدا لاسم إن فيكون منصوب المحل

SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r2.claim: Alternatively أنت is a subject, العليم الحكيم its predicate, and the whole clause predicates إن.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r2.anchor: وأن يكون مبتدأ خبره ما بعده والجملة خبر إن

SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r3.claim: أنت may be فصل; grammarians dispute whether it has case and whether case follows the preceding word as al-Farrāʾ says or the following as al-Kisāʾī says.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r3.anchor: وأن يكون فصلا، وفيه الخلاف المشهور، وهل له محل إعراب أم لا

SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r4.claim: الحكيم may be a second predicate or adjective of العليم; both are فعيل with intensive force beyond the ordinary active participle.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r4.anchor: و " الحكيم " خبر ثان أو صفة للعليم، وهما فعيل بمعنى فاعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r5.claim: حكم means precision and preventing departure from intent; the animal's bridle is حكمة for restraint, and Jarīr's أحكموا witnesses restraint.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r5.anchor: والحكم لغة: الإتقان والمنع من الخروج عن الإرادة، ومنه حكمة الدابة

SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r6.claim: العليم precedes الحكيم because علم and لا علم لنا have appeared, and wisdom derives from knowledge.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r6.anchor: وقدم " العليم " على " الحكيم " لأنه هو المتصل به في قوله

SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r7.claim: الحكيم is an attribute of essence as possessing wisdom, and an attribute of action as perfecting His workmanship.
SAMIN-DURR:2:32#3/r7.anchor: والحكيم صفة ذات إن فسر بذي الحكمة، وصفة فعل إن فسر بأنه المحكم لصنعته

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f3.claim: The comparison test establishes Adam's superiority over the angels and shows that they are not suited to earthly vicegerency as he is.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f3.anchor: ثم ذكر اختبار المفاضلة الذي أجراه بين آدم والملائكة ففضلهم فيه آدم، وثبت لهم فيه أنهم ليسوا أهلاً للاستخلاف في الأرض بخلاف آدم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f7.claim: Teaching Adam all the names honors him by giving him knowledge the angels do not possess.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f7.anchor: تفضيل آدم على الملائكة بتعليمه الأسماء كلها مما لا يعلمه الملائكة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f9.claim: The story establishes God's comprehensive knowledge, denies the angels knowledge except what He teaches them, and gives Adam knowledge fit for the vicegerency.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f9.anchor: نفي العلم عن الملائكة إلا ما عَلَّمهم إياه ربُّ العزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r1.claim: A report says that when Adam was created, angels expected God would make no creation more knowledgeable or honored than them; God then showed them Adam's knowledge and honor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r1.anchor: روي أن الملائكة حين خلق الله آدم قالت: يخلق ربنا ما شاء، فلن يخلق خلقا أعلم منا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r9.claim: The angels' سبحانك disavows making a claim or objecting to God's wisdom.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r9.anchor: قالوا سبحانك لا علم لنا: أي تنزيهك عن الادعاء وعن الاعتراض.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r10.claim: He reports an unusual proposal that سبحانك is a reduplicated dual-like form meaning repeated glorification, but rejects it because it entails an unattested singular سبحا and other grammatical difficulties.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r10.anchor: وقيل: معناه تنزيه لك بعد تنزيه لفظه لفظ تثنية، والمعنى كذلك كما قالوا في لبيك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r11.claim: The kaf in سبحانك is an object, though some allow it as subject on the sense you are transcendent; Abu Hayyan maintains it is an accusative verbal noun with an obligatorily omitted cognate verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r11.anchor: والكاف في سبحانك مفعول به أضيف إليه. وأجاز بعضهم أن يكون فاعلا، لأن المعنى تنزهت.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r12.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r12.claim: Al-Kisa'i analyzes سبحانك as an annexed vocative, which Abu Hayyan rejects because no vocative particle before it is transmitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r12.anchor: وزعم الكسائي أنه منادى مضاف، ويبطله أنه لا يحفظ دخول حرف النداء عليه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r13.claim: Because the angels had earlier questioned appointing a potentially corrupt creation, they begin with glorification as apology and courtesy, then use لا with an indefinite noun to deny every kind of knowledge except what God taught.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r13.anchor: ولما سأل تعالى الملائكة، ولم يكن عندهم علم بالجواب، وكانوا قد سبق منهم قولهم: أتجعل فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r14.claim: Their answer models complete humility and surrender to God, the first teacher, by disclaiming knowledge and accepting only what he taught.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p237/r14.anchor: ثم استثنوا من ذلك ما علمهم هو تعالى، فقالوا: إلا ما علمتنا، وهذا غاية في ترك الدعوى والاستسلام التام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r1.claim: Their speech begins a fresh answer to the implied question whether they fulfilled the task assigned to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r1.anchor: استئناف واقع موقع الجواب كأنه قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r2.claim: When successive statements introduced by “they said” are ordered in meaning, the clearest usage omits a conjunction; this is frequent in al-Shuʿarāʾ and throughout the Qurʾān.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r2.anchor: الجمل المفتتحة بالقول إذا كانت مرتبا بعضها على بعض في المعنى فالأصح أن لا يؤتي فيها بحرف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r3.claim: One view takes subḥān as a verbal noun from sabbaḥa, meaning to declare transcendent; it is normally construct and accusative after an obligatorily implicit verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r3.anchor: قيل : إنه مصدر وفعله سبح مخففا بمعنى نزه ولا يكاد يستعمل إلا مضافا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r4.claim: The cited poetry includes rare unconstructed forms and even uses sabbaḥa as a verb, illustrating the unusual usage of the word.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226/r4.anchor: سبحانه ثم سبحانا نعوذ به وقبلنا سبح الجودي والجمد شاذ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.speaker: الكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī's claim that subḥān is a vocative has no supporting proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.anchor: ومجيئه منادي مما زعمه الكسائي ولا حجة له

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.speaker: جماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.claim: A group treats subḥān as the proper name of glorification rather than a verbal noun, to avoid circularity and distinguish the spoken form from its meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى أنه علم للتسبيح بمعنى التنزيه لا مصدر سبح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.claim: The group cites a poem about saying subḥān when al-ʿAlqama's boast arrived; opponents answer that Allah is omitted in an understood construct, leaving subḥān in its usual form.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.anchor: قد قلت لما جاءني فخره سبحان من علقمة الفاخر إذ لولا أنه علم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.speaker: بعض
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.claim: An unusual proposal glosses subḥānaka as repeated sanctification, like labbayka; Al-Ālūsī objects that this would require a dual, nominative form and an unexplained fixed nūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.anchor: ومن الغريب قول بعض : إن معنى ( سبحانك ) تنزيه لك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r5.claim: Their answer admits inability to know the names and inability to discharge the succession task, since God had not taught them those names.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r5.anchor: والغرض من هذا الحواب الاعتراف بالعجز عن أمر الخلافة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r6.claim: Their words imply that they know only through teaching; because they had learned the wisdom of succession too, their earlier question was inquiry, not objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r6.anchor: وفيه آعار بأن سؤالهم لم يكن إلا استفسارا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r7.claim: They praise God's teaching with humility and proper courtesy, avoiding self-assertion; they do not narrowly say that they lack knowledge of the names.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r7.anchor: وثناء عليه تعالى بما أفاض عليهم مع غاية التواضع ومراعاة الأدب وترك الدعوى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r8.speaker: من زعم عدم العصمة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r8.claim: Those who deny the speakers' infallibility treat this as repentance; Al-Ālūsī says it resembles repentance, but for leaving what was preferable, not a breach of infallibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r8.anchor: ومن زعم عدم العصمة جعل هذا توبة والإنصاف أنه يشبهها ولكن لا عن ذنب مخل بالعصمة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r9.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r9.claim: Most grammarians take mā as a relative pronoun with an omitted antecedent, either in apposition or accusative as an exception.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r9.anchor: عند الجمهور موصولة حذف عائدها وهي إما في موضع رفع على البدل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r10.speaker: ابن عطية عن الزهراوي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports al-Zahrawī's parse: mā is accusative with ʿallamtanā; a strained defense makes the exception disconnected and mā conditional with an omitted response.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r10.anchor: وحكى إبن عطية عن الزهراوي أنها في موضع نصب ب ( علمتنا )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r11.claim: The final declaration confirms their denial of their own knowledge by affirming God's perfect knowledge and wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r11.anchor: تذييل يؤكد مضمون الجملة السابقة ولما نفوا العلم عن أنفسهم أثبتوه لله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r12.claim: Ḥikma derives from restraint: knowledge prevents false acts, while precise action prevents corruption and objection; this latter sense avoids repeating “all-knowing.”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r12.anchor: وأصل الحكمة المنع ومنه حكمة الدابة لأنها تمنعها عن الاعوجاج ويقال للعلم لأنه يمنع عن ارتكاب الباطل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r13.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r13.claim: Abū Ḥayyān gives two readings of al-ḥakīm: possessor of wisdom, an attribute of essence, or one whose creations are perfected, an attribute of action.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r13.anchor: وهو على الأول صفة ذات وعلى الثاني صفة فعل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r14.claim: The familiar distinction is that al-ḥakīm as all-knowing names an essence attribute, while acting without objection names an action attribute; both terms are unqualified here.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r14.anchor: والمشهور أنه إن أريد به ( العليم ) كان من صفات الذات أو الفاعل لما لا اعتراض عليه كان من صفات الفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r15.claim: Knowledge precedes wisdom because the passage has just mentioned “inform Me” and “we have no knowledge,” and wisdom follows knowledge; the ending counters a possible misreading of their opening.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r15.anchor: لمناسبة ما تقدم من ( أنبؤني ) و ( لا علم لنا )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r16.claim: Anta may be a separator that emphasizes the predicate and its restrictive force, an emphatic pronoun, or the subject with what follows as predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r16.anchor: و ( أنت ) يحتمل أن يكون فصلا لا محل له على المشهور

ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p226#2/r17.claim: The objects of both attributes are omitted to convey unrestricted scope; restricting them to commands and decrees is possible, but generality is better.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p80/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p80/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p80/r2.claim: The angels mean that God is too exalted for them to encompass anything of His knowledge except what He has taught them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p80/r2.anchor: معناه فإنك أجل من أن نحيط بشيء من علمك إلا ما علمتنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p80/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p80/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p80/r3.claim: Al-ʿAlīm means the One who knows His creation.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p80/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p80/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p80/r4.claim: Al-Ḥakīm can mean the just judge, or the One who makes matters firm against corruption; its root sense is restraint, as a bridle restrains an animal from straying.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p80/r4.anchor: والحكيم له معنيان: أحدهما الحاكم وهو القاضي العدل والثاني المحكم للأمر كي لا يتطرق إليه الفساد وأصل الحكمة في اللغة: المنع

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r1.claim: The angels admit their limitation, show their question was inquiry rather than objection, recognize the revealed human excellence and wisdom of creation, thank God for teaching them, and defer all knowledge to Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r1.anchor: اعتراف بالعجز والقصور، وإشعار بأن سؤالهم كان استفسارا ولم يكن اعتراضا، وأنه قد بان لهم ما خفي عليهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r2.claim: Subḥān is a verbal noun like ghufrān, almost always used in an accusative construct with its verb understood, as in maʿādh Allāh; a poet exceptionally uses it as a predicate noun for glorification.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r2.anchor: وسبحان: مصدر كغفران ولا يكاد يستعمل إلا مضافا منصوبا بإضمار فعله، كمعاذ الله.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r3.claim: Beginning with subḥān apologizes for inquiry and ignorance; it likewise opens repentance in Moses' words in 7:143 and Jonah's in 21:87.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r3.anchor: وتصدير الكلام به اعتذار عن الاستفسار والجهل بحقيقة الحال، ولذلك جعل مفتاح التوبة فقال موسى عليه السلام:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r4.claim: Al-ʿAlīm means that nothing is hidden from God; al-Ḥakīm means He perfectly orders His creations and acts only with profound wisdom.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r4.anchor: العليم } الذي لا يخفي عليه خافية. { الحكيم } المحكم لمبدعاته الذي لا يفعل إلا ما فيه حكمة بالغة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r5.claim: Anta may be a separating pronoun or emphasis on the attached second-person pronoun, a use allowed to a dependent element but not as a standalone object; alternatively it is the subject of a clause predicated of inna.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33/r5.anchor: وأنت فصل، وقيل: تأكيد للكاف كما في قولك: مررت بك أنت، وإن لم يجز: مررت بأنت،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r2.claim: After Adam informs the angels, God's question restates 2:30 in fuller form as evidence: He knows hidden matters of heaven and earth and their outward and inward conditions, including what they did not know.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r2.anchor: استحضار لقوله تعالى: إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون [البقرة: 30] لكنه جاء به على وجه أبسط ليكون كالحجة عليه،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r7.claim: The passage establishes human nobility and the superiority of knowledge to worship; knowledge is a condition and central qualification for vicegerency, and Adam's greater knowledge makes him superior to the angels, as 39:9 states.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r7.anchor: واعلم أن هذه الآيات تدل على شرف الإنسان، ومزية العلم وفضله على العبادة، وأنه شرط في الخلافة بل العمدة فيها،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r8.claim: Teaching may be attributed to God, though al-Muʿallim is not used as His title because it denotes someone who practices teaching professionally.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r8.anchor: وأن التعليم يصح إسناده إلى الله تعالى، وإن لم يصح إطلاق المعلم عليه لاختصاصه بمن يحترف به،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r9.claim: The verse supports divinely instituted languages: teaching the names means conveying words with their meanings, which presupposes prior designation; since no one before Adam could have designated them, God did so.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r9.anchor: وأن اللغات توقيفية، فإن الأسماء تدل على الألفاظ بخصوص أو عموم، وتعليمها ظاهر في إلقائها على المتعلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r10.claim: Wisdom is a concept beyond knowledge; otherwise the pairing All-Knowing, All-Wise would be redundant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r10.anchor: وأن مفهوم الحكمة زائد على مفهوم العلم وإلا لتكرر قوله: { إنك أنت العليم الحكيم }

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r11.claim: The angels' knowledge and perfections can increase, contrary to philosophers who deny increase for the highest angelic rank and interpret 37:164 as fixing each one's station.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r11.anchor: وأن علوم الملائكة وكمالاتهم تقبل الزيادة، والحكماء منعوا ذلك في الطبقة العليا منهم،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r12.claim: God knows things before they come into existence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:32-33#2/r12.anchor: وأنه تعالى يعلم الأشياء قبل حدوثها.

IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains saying “Glory be to God” as declaring Him free of evil.

IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r2.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r2.claim: When Umar asks its meaning, Ali says it is a word God loves for Himself and loves people to say.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r2.anchor: ثم قال عمر لعلي واصحابه عنده : لا اله الا الله قد عرفناه ، فما سبحان الله ؟ فقال له علي : كلمة احبها الله لنفسه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r3.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r3.claim: Maimun ibn Mihran says it is a name by which God is magnified and declared free of evil.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r3.anchor: سال رجل ميمون بن مهران عن سبحان الله . فقال : اسم يعظم الله به ويحاشى به من السوء .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says “Glory be to God” is a name people cannot claim for themselves.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r4.anchor: عن الحسن قال : سبحان الله اسم لا يستطيع الناس ان ينتحلوه .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r5.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r5.claim: They answer only about what God taught them; what He did not teach, He knows better than they do.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r5.anchor: عن ابن اسحاق : قالوا سبحانك لا علم لنا الا ما علمتنا انك انت العليم الحكيم اي انما اجبناك فيما علمتنا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r6.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r6.claim: Al-ʿAlim means that God knows what they conceal.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r6.anchor: وبه عن سلمة ثنا محمد بن اسحاق : العليم اي عليم بما تخفون .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r7.claim: Abu al-Aliya says al-Hakim means wise in His command.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r7.anchor: عن أبي العالية : قوله : الحكيم قال : حكيم في امره .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r8.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r8.claim: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr says al-Hakim means wise in His argument and proof to His servants.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p81/r8.anchor: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير قوله : الحكيم قال : الحكيم في عذره وحجته إلى عباده .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r1.claim: The particle fa is absent from qālū because this is direct dialogue, as in the angels' speech in 2:30.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r1.anchor: من الفاء لأنه محاورة كما تقدم عند قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r2.claim: The angels begin with glorification to observe proper reverence before the possessor of absolute majesty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r2.anchor: وافتتاح كلامهم بالتسبيح وقوف في مقام الأدب والتعظيم لذي العظمة المطلقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r3.claim: Subḥān is the verbal noun of tasbīḥ and is not a regular verbal noun of the doubled verb; another analysis derives it from a lighter sabbaḥa meaning to declare God transcendent, like ghufrān and shukrān.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r3.anchor: وهو اسم مصدر سبح المضاعف وليس مصدرا لأنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r4.claim: Subḥān is usually an accusative absolute with an implicit verb, as in maʿādh Allāh, though rare constructions occur.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r4.anchor: وقد كثر استعماله منصوبا على المفعولية المطلقة بإضمار فعله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r5.claim: Its conventional use as a name for transcendence made it a lexicalized generic proper noun; al-Nābigha's line uses Barra and Fijār as analogous names.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r5.anchor: فصار سبحان كالعلم الجنسي مثل برة وفجار بكسر الراء في قول النابغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r6.speaker: سيبويه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r6.claim: Sībawayh explains that subḥān takes no tanwīn because speakers came to treat it as definite.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r7.claim: The angels are not informing God of their condition or stating a fact He does not know; their statement is an admission of incapacity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r7.anchor: خبر مراد منه الاعتراف بالعجز لا الإخبار عن حالهم لأنهم يوقنون أن الله يعلم ما تضمنه كلامهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r8.claim: Angelic knowledge is limited to what God inspires or commands and cannot grow by inference: angels receive meanings but do not independently derive them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r8.anchor: كلامهم هذا يدل على أن علومهم محدودة غير قابلة للزيادة فهي مقصورة على ما ألهمهم الله تعالى وما يأمرهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r9.claim: Opening with subḥānaka implicitly apologizes for the angels' earlier question in 2:30 and displays respect before the explicit admission of ignorance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r9.anchor: فهو افتتاح من قبيل براعة الاستهلال عن الاعتذار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r10.claim: The statement that God is all-knowing and wise explains their limited knowledge: a creator who knows and perfectly orders creation did not grant them knowledge beyond their capacity; the prefixed inna signals explanation, not mere praise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p413/r10.anchor: والذي دل على أن هذا القول مسوق للتعليل وليس مجرد ثناء هو تصديره بإن في غير مقام رد إنكار ولا تردد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r1.claim: The excerpt includes an unattributed poetic line containing al-samīʿ in the grammatical discussion; it does not identify the poet or state the specific feature witnessed by this line.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r1.anchor: أمن ريحانة الداعي السميع يؤرقني وأصحابي هجوع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r2.claim: An anonymous line recited by Abū ʿAlī uses al-umm al-najība to mean a mother who gives birth, as the contrast with a father who did not beget shows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r2.anchor: ما أنشده أبو علي ولم يعزه : فمن يك لم ينجب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r3.claim: The Qurʾānic description badīʿ al-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ in 2:117 supports natural adjective-pattern variation; there is no need to read the definite article as a substitute for a possessive or to force ḥakīm to mean possessor of wisdom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r3.anchor: والعرب تجري أوزان بعض المشتقات على بعض فلا حاجة إلى التكلف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r4.claim: Following ʿalīm with ḥakīm adds a more specific perfection: wisdom exceeds knowledge, like calling someone an eloquent or accomplished poet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r4.anchor: وتعقيب العليم بالحكيم من إتباع الوصف بأخص منه فإن مفهوم الحكمة زائد على مفهوم العلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r5.speaker: الشيخ لطف الله الأرضرومي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r5.claim: Lutf Allāh al-Arḍarūmī defines divine wisdom as knowing a thing and perfecting its creation and governance according to the governed being's capacity, with insight into realities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r5.anchor: للشيخ لطف الله الأرضرومي : وفي الحكيم ذو الحكمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r6.speaker: أبو حامد الغزالي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r6.claim: Al-Ghazālī says God alone is truly wise: He knows the noblest object through the noblest, eternal knowledge, perfectly matching what is known without obscurity or doubt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r6.anchor: وقال أبو حامد الغزالي في ( المقصد الأسنى ) : الحكيم ذو الحكمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r7.claim: Anta is a pronoun of separation, and placing it here is one of the constructions that conveys restriction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r7.anchor: ضمير فصل ، وتوسيطه من صيغ القصر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r8.claim: The restriction may correct the angels' implied belief that they possessed knowledge and wisdom, or be figurative restriction to God's complete knowledge and wisdom alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r8.anchor: فالمعنى قصر العلم والحكمة على الله قصر قلب لردهم اعتقادهم أنفسهم أنهم على جانب من علم وحكمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r9.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr defers further discussion of wisdom to 2:269.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p415/r9.anchor: وسيجيء الكلام على الحكمة عند قوله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the language scholars agree that tasbih means declaring God exalted above every defect.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج لا اختلاف بين أهل اللغة أن التسبيح هو التنزيه لله تعالى عن كل سوء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r2.claim: Al-ʿAlim means the one who knows; its faʿil form intensifies the sense.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r2.anchor: والعليم بمعنى العالم جاء على بناء فعيل للمبالغة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba takes al-Hakim to mean the judge.
