IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r3.anchor: وفي الحكيم قولان أحدهما أنه بمعنى الحاكم قاله ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r4.speaker: الخطابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p63#2/r4.claim: Al-Khattabi takes al-Hakim to mean the one who perfects things.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r1.claim: The angels sanctify God, acknowledging that no one encompasses His knowledge and that they know only what He teaches them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r1.anchor: هذا تقديس وتنزيه من الملائكة لله تعالى أن يحيط أحد بشيء من علمه إلا بما شاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r2.claim: God knows everything and is wise in creation, command, teaching whom He wills, and withholding from whom He wills; His wisdom and justice are complete.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r2.anchor: أي: العليم بكل شيء، الحكيم في خلقك وأمرك وفي تعليمك من تشاء ومنعك من تشاء، لك الحكمة في ذلك، والعدل التام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains tasbih as God’s declaring Himself free of evil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: سبحان الله، قال: تنزيه الله نفسه عن السوء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r4.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r4.claim: When Umar asks Ali what Subhan Allah means, Ali says it is a word God loves and has chosen for Himself, and loves people to say.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r4.anchor: فقال له علي: كلمة أحبها الله لنفسه، ورضيها، وأحب أن تقال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r5.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r5.claim: Maymun ibn Mihran defines Subhan Allah as a name that magnifies God and declares Him free of evil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p225/r5.anchor: سأل رجل ميمون بن مهران عن "سبحان الله"، فقال: اسم يعظم الله به

JISHUMI:v1p322/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p322/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p322/r1.claim: Ḥikma is opposite folly; iḥkām means making something exact and free of defect, and its root sense is preventing corruption.
JISHUMI:v1p322/r1.anchor: الحكمة: نقيض السفه، والإحكام: الإتقان، يقال: أحكم عمله إذا بالغ فيه فأصاب حقيقته

JISHUMI:v1p322/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p322/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p322/r2.claim: When ḥakīm means knowing, it is an essential attribute of God.
JISHUMI:v1p322/r2.anchor: ويوصف الله تعالى بأنه حكيم لوجهين: بمعنى عليم، فيكون صفة لذاته

JISHUMI:v1p322/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p322/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p322/r3.claim: When ḥakīm means one who makes His acts sound and exact, it describes an attribute of action.
JISHUMI:v1p322/r3.anchor: وبمعنى محكم لأفعاله فيكون في صفات الفعل

JISHUMI:v1p322/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p322/r4.speaker: الخليل
JISHUMI:v1p322/r4.claim: Al-Khalīl parses subḥānaka as an accusative verbal noun with an understood verb meaning we glorify Your transcendence.
JISHUMI:v1p322/r4.anchor: سبحانك: نصب على المصدر، أي نسبح سبحانك، عن الخليل

JISHUMI:v1p322/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p322/r5.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p322/r5.claim: Another parse makes subḥānaka a vocative, O Transcendence.
JISHUMI:v1p322/r5.anchor: وقيل: على النداء أي يا سبحانك

JISHUMI:v1p322/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p322/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p322/r6.claim: The kāf in innaka is accusative as the subject of inna; its predicate is anta al-ʿalīm al-ḥakīm.
JISHUMI:v1p322/r6.anchor: والكاف في قوله: إنك محله نصب؛ لأنه اسم (إن) وخبره: أنت العليم الحكيم

JISHUMI:v1p322/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p322/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p322/r7.anchor: ثم بين تعالى جواب الملائكة فقال: قالوا أي الملائكة سبحانك

JISHUMI:v1p322/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p322/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p322/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the angels declare God transcendent from anyone besides Him knowing the unseen.
JISHUMI:v1p322/r8.anchor: قيل: تنزيها لك من أن يعلم الغيب سواك، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p322/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p322/r9.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p322/r9.claim: Abū ʿAlī says they use reverent language to declare God free of anything blameworthy even though they do not know the wisdom of His acts.
JISHUMI:v1p322/r9.anchor: عن أبي علي. لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا

JISHUMI:v1p322/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p322/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p322/r10.claim: The angels lacked knowledge of the names being asked about because God had not taught them; the concise wording means these names were not among what He taught them.
JISHUMI:v1p322/r10.anchor: يعني لا علم لنا بما سألنا عنه من هذه الأسماء؛ إذ لم يكن فيها علمهم

JISHUMI:v1p322/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p322/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p322/r11.claim: They could have said they did not know these names, but their wording glorifies God, acknowledges that their knowledge comes from Him, thanks Him, and fulfills their duty.
JISHUMI:v1p322/r11.anchor: ولو قيل: لا علم لنا بهذا لكان جوابا صحيحا غير أن في هذا الذي أجابوا تغظيما لله تعالى

JISHUMI:v1p322/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p322/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p322/r12.claim: God knows without being taught, unlike the angels whose knowledge is received from Him.
JISHUMI:v1p322/r12.anchor: قيل: أنت العليم من غير تعليم؛ لأنهم أثبتوا له ما نفوه عن أنفسهم

BURSEVI:v1p75/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p75/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p75/r1.claim: Adam's first distinction is that he succeeds all creatures, while none can succeed him: he gathers the spiritual, bodily, celestial, earthly, worldly, and other realms, and alone received the honor of God's spirit, as 17:70 states.
BURSEVI:v1p75/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنه يخلف عن جميع المخلوقات ولا يخلفه المكونات بأسرها وذلك لأن الله جمع فيه ما في العوالم كلها من الروحانيات

BURSEVI:v1p75/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p75/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p75/r2.claim: Adam's second distinction is to represent God in outward sign and inward meaning: human existence points to its maker as a building to its builder, and human unity and attributes mirror the divine attributes.
BURSEVI:v1p75/r2.anchor: والثاني : أنه يخلف وينوب عن الله صورة ومعنى أما صورة فوجوده في الظاهر يخلف عن وجود الحق في الحقيقة

BURSEVI:v1p75/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p75/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p75/r3.claim: No other creature fully represents God: animals lack knowledge of their maker, and angels know Him but cannot know themselves and all His attributes completely; humanity alone knows itself through caliphate and all divine names.
BURSEVI:v1p75/r3.anchor: وأما الحيوانات فإنها وإن كان لها بعض هذه الصفات ولكن ليس لها علم بوجود موجدها وأما الملائكة فإنهم وإن كانوا عالمين بوجود موجدهم

BURSEVI:v1p75/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p75/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p75/r4.claim: The human inward lamp consists of the secret in the heart's glass, set in the body's niche, with the spirit as oil; when God's beauty manifests, the lamp shines and the human vicegerent displays divine attributes through just and merciful action, as 38:26, 9:128, and 48:29 show.
BURSEVI:v1p75/r4.anchor: وأما معنى فليس في العالم مصباح يستضيء بنار نور الله فيظهر أنوار صفاته في الأرض خلافة عنه إلا مصباح الإنسان

BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r1.claim: Qālū resumes the narrative as the answer to whether the angels discharged their charge; subḥānaka declares God free of any unbefitting quality, including purposeless or unwise acts.
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r1.anchor: {قالوا} استئناف واقع موقع الجواب كأنه قيل فماذا قالوا حينئذ هل خرجوا من عهدة ما كلفوه أو لا

BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r2.claim: Subḥān is a verbal noun used in place of the verb, usually annexed; when unannexed it becomes a proper name for glorification and is indeclinable because it is definite and ends in alif-nūn.
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r2.anchor: وسبحان اسم واقع موقع المصدر لا يكاد يستعمل إلا مضافا فإذا أفرد عن الإضافة كان إسما علما للتسبيح لا ينصرف للتعريف والألف والنون

BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r3.claim: The formula precedes repentance in Moses' declaration, 7:143, and Jonah's confession, 21:87.
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r3.anchor: وهي كلمة تقدم على التوبة قال موسى عليه السلام : {سبحانك تبت إليك} (الأعراف : 143)

BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r4.claim: The angels admit their inability and clarify that their earlier question sought explanation, not objection: they know only what God taught within their capacity and could receive nothing beyond their readiness.
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r4.anchor: {لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا} اعتراف منهم بالعجز عما كلفوه وإشعار بأن سؤالهم كان استفسارا ولم يكن اعتراضا

BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r5.claim: Mā is a verbal noun: except knowledge that You taught us; the phrase is nominative as a substitute for the position of lā ʿilm, and anta in innaka anta is a separating pronoun.
BURSEVI:v1p79#2/r5.anchor: وما مصدرية أي : إلا علما علمتناه ومحله رفع بدل من موضع لا علم

BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r1.claim: Al-ʿAlīm is the one from whom nothing hidden is concealed; this affirms God's statement that He knows what the angels do not, in 2:30.
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r1.anchor: {العليم} الذي لا يخفى عليه خافية وهذه إشارة إلى تحقيقهم لقوله تعالى : {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون}

BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r2.claim: Al-Ḥakīm is the one who perfects His creations and acts only with profound wisdom.
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r2.anchor: {الحكيم} المحكم لمبتدعاته والذي لا يفعل إلا ما فيه حكمة بالغة

BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r3.claim: The verse teaches servants to remember their limitations and God's favor, to say “I do not know” without shame when ignorant, and not conceal what they know.
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r3.anchor: وأفادت الآية أن العبد ينبغي له أن لا يغفل عن نقصانه وعن فضل الله وإحسانه ولا يأنف أن يقول لا أعلم فيما لا يعلم

BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r4.speaker: أبو يوسف
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r4.claim: When people challenged Abu Yusuf for drawing a public salary while answering a question with “I do not know,” he replied that he was paid for his knowledge; payment for his ignorance would exceed the world's wealth.
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r4.anchor: وسئل أبو يوسف القاضي عن مسألة فقال : لا أدري فقالوا له ترتزق من بيت المال كل يوم كذا كذا ثم تقول لا أدري

BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r5.speaker: عالم
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r5.claim: A scholar on a pulpit answered a question with “I do not know”; when told a pulpit was no place for the ignorant, he said that greater ignorance would have raised him to the sky.
BURSEVI:v1p79#3/r5.anchor: وحكي أن عالما سئل عن مسألة وهو فوق المنبر فقال : لا أدري فقيل له : ليس المنبر موضع الجهال

MUQATIL:2:32/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:32/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:32/r1.claim: The speakers are the angels, who glorify God and acknowledge that they know only what He taught them.
MUQATIL:2:32/r1.anchor: قالوا } قالت الملائكة { سبحانك لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا

MUQATIL:2:32/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:32/r2.speaker: الله عز وجل
MUQATIL:2:32/r2.claim: God challenges the angels for claiming knowledge of what had not yet been created or seen when they do not know even what they see.
MUQATIL:2:32/r2.anchor: قال الله عز وجل لهم: كيف تدعون العلم فيما لم يخلق بعد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r1.claim: The angels declare God beyond anything being hidden from Him and beyond objection to His governance.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r1.anchor: تنزيها لك أن يخفى عليك شيء أو عن الاعتراض عليك فى تدبيرك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r2.claim: The verse shows that knowledge of the names surpasses what is attainable through worship; knowledge of the divine law is all the more so.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r2.anchor: فكيف بعلم الشريعة انتصابه على المصدر تقديره سبحت الله تسبيحا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r3.claim: Subḥāna is accusative as a cognate verbal noun, with the implied phrase ‘I glorify God with glorification.’
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r3.anchor: انتصابه على المصدر تقديره سبحت الله تسبيحا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r4.claim: Mā means ‘that which’ and ʿilm means ‘known object’: we know nothing except what You taught us.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r4.anchor: أى لا معلوم لنا إلى الذى علمتنا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r5.claim: Al-ʿAlīm is the one who is not taught; al-Ḥakīm is wise in what He decrees and determines.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r5.anchor: غير المعلم ﴿ الحكيم ﴾ فيما قضيت وقدرت

NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r6.claim: The kāf may be ism inna and anta the subject of a clause with two predicates; alternatively, anta is a separator and the two names are predicates.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p37/r6.anchor: أنت فصل والخبر العلم والحكيم خبر ثان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r1.claim: The angels’ “Glory be to You” declares God exalted above anyone else knowing the unseen.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { قالوا سبحانك لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا } فيه ثلاث مسائل:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r2.claim: The angels answer “inform Me” by admitting they know only what God taught them and do not pretend to knowledge they lack.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r2.anchor: وهذا جوابهم عن قوله: «أنبئوني» فأجابوا أنهم لا يعلمون إلا ما أعلمهم به

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r3.claim: Ma in “what You taught us” may be a relative pronoun meaning “that which,” or a verbal noun meaning “Your teaching of us.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r3.anchor: و «ما» في «ما علمتنا» بمعنى الذي أي إلا الذي علمتنا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r4.claim: Anyone asked about something unknown should say “God knows best” or “I do not know,” following angels, prophets, and leading scholars.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r4.anchor: الواجب على من سئل عن علم أن يقول إن لم يعلم: الله أعلم ولا أدري، اقتداء بالملائكة والأنبياء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r5.speaker: الصادق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r5.claim: The truthful one (the Prophet) warned that with scholars’ deaths knowledge is taken, leaving ignorant people to issue opinions that mislead themselves and others.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r5.anchor: لكن قد أخبر الصادق أن بموت العلماء يقبض العلم فيبقى ناس جهال يستفتون فيفتون برأيهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r6.claim: Ibn Umar reports that when asked which places are worst, the Prophet first said he did not know until asking Gabriel; Gabriel then asked Michael, who answered that mosques are best and markets worst.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r6.anchor: فروى البستي في المسند الصحيح له عن ابن عمر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r7.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r7.claim: When asked about a grandmother’s inheritance, Abu Bakr told her to return while he asked people.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r7.anchor: وقال الصديق للجدة: ارجعي حتى أسأل الناس.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r8.claim: Ali says the most heart-soothing words, repeated three times, are for a person asked what he does not know to say, “God knows best.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r8.anchor: وكان علي يقول: وأبردها على الكبد ثلاث مرات. قالوا وما ذلك يا أمير المؤمنين؟

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r9.claim: Asked a question, Ibn Umar answered that he did not know; afterward he praised the answer as proper humility.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r9.anchor: وسأل ابن عمر رجل عن مسألة فقال: لا علم لي بها فلما أدبر الرجل. قال ابن عمر:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r10.speaker: يحيى بن سعيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r10.claim: Yahya ibn Saʿid rebukes Qasim for lacking an answer on religion despite being descended from the two rightly guided leaders, Abu Bakr and Umar.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r10.anchor: فقال يحيى للقاسم: يا أبا محمد إنه قبيح على مثلك عظيم أن يسأل عن شيء من أمر هذا الدين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r11.speaker: القاسم بن عبيد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r11.claim: In a Muslim report, Qasim answers Yahya ibn Saʿid that speaking without knowledge or relying on an untrustworthy source is worse than being unable to answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r11.anchor: قال يقول له القاسم: أقبح من ذاك عند من عقل عن الله أن أقول بغير علم أو آخذ عن غير ثقة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r12.speaker: ابن هرمز
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r12.claim: Ibn Hurmuz says a scholar should leave “I do not know” as a legacy so students will use it when unsure.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r12.anchor: وقال مالك بن أنس: سمعت ابن هرمز يقول: ينبغي للعالم أن يورث جلساءه من بعده لا أدري

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r13.speaker: مالك بن أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r13.claim: Haytham ibn Jamil witnessed Malik answer “I do not know” to thirty-two of the forty-eight questions he was asked.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r13.anchor: وذكر الهيثم بن جميل قال: شهدت مالك بن أنس سئل عن ثمان وأربعين مسألة فقال في اثنتين وثلاثين منها: لا أدري.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r14.claim: Al-Qurtubi says such examples from early Muslims are abundant; refusing to admit ignorance stems from seeking status and lacking fairness in learning.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32/r14.anchor: قلت: ومثله كثير عن الصحابة والتابعين وفقهاء المسلمين، وإنما يحمل على ترك ذلك الرياسة وعدم الإنصاف في العلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r1.speaker: ابن عبد البر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr calls fairness a blessing and etiquette of learning; without fairness, one neither understands nor seeks understanding.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عبد البر: من بركة العلم وآدابه الإنصاف فيه، ومن لم ينصف لم يفهم ولم يتفهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r2.speaker: مالك ابن أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r2.claim: Mālik ibn Anas said fairness was exceptionally scarce in his own era.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r2.anchor: سمعت ابن وهب يقول سمعت مالك ابن أنس يقول: ما في زماننا شيء أقل من الإنصاف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r3.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says the present is worse: corruption is widespread, and many seek knowledge for status and to defeat rivals in disputation, hardening hearts and undermining piety.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r3.anchor: قلت: هذا في زمن مالك فكيف في زماننا اليوم الذي عم فينا الفساد وكثر فيه الطغام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r4.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r4.claim: When ʿUmar proposed capping dowries at forty ūqiyyas and placing any excess in the treasury, a woman cited 4:20; he admitted she was right and he was wrong.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r4.anchor: أين هذا مما روي عن عمر رضي الله عنه وقد قال: لا تزيدوا في مهور النساء على أربعين أوقية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r5.speaker: امرأة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r5.claim: A woman challenged ʿUmar's proposed dowry cap by citing the Qurʾānic allowance of a large dowry; he accepted her correction.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r5.anchor: فقامت امرأة من صوب النساء طويلة فيها فطس فقالت: ما ذلك لك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r6.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r6.claim: A man corrected ʿAlī on a question; ʿAlī accepted the correction and said that above every learned person is someone more learned.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال: سأل رجل عليا رضي الله عنه عن مسألة فقال فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r7.speaker: قاسم بن أصبغ
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r7.claim: Qāsim ibn Aṣbagh recounts that Bakkār ibn Ḥammād accepted a correction: the report says مجتابي النمار, referring to people wearing front-slit garments, not مجتابي الثمار.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#2/r7.anchor: وذكر أبو محمد قاسم بن أصبغ قال: لما رحلت إلى المشرق نزلت القيروان فأخذت على بكر بن حماد حديث مسدد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r1.speaker: يزيد بن الوليد بن عبد الملك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r1.claim: Yazīd ibn al-Walīd's poem advises speaking only within one's knowledge and falling silent when knowledge is exhausted.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r1.anchor: إذا ما تحدثت في مجلس تناهى حديثي إلى ما علمت ولم أعد علمي إلى غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r2.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r2.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh parse سبحانَكَ as an accusative verbal noun conveying I glorify You with glorification.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r2.anchor: «سبحان» منصوب على المصدر عند الخليل وسيبويه، يؤدي عن معنى نسبحك تسبيحا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r3.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī instead parses سبحانَكَ as an accusative vocative in an annexed construction.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r3.anchor: وقال الكسائي: هو منصوب على أنه نداء مضاف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r4.claim: Al-ʿAlīm is an intensive form indicating the abundance of what God knows among His creatures.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r4.anchor: و { العليم } فعيل للمبالغة والتكثير في المعلومات في خلق الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r5.claim: One explanation of al-Ḥakīm is al-Ḥākim, the judge or ruler, with added intensity in the form.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r5.anchor: و { الحكيم } معناه الحاكم وبينهما مزيد المبالغة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī explains al-Ḥakīm as the One who makes things firm; on this account it is an attribute of action.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r6.anchor: وقيل معناه المحكم ويجيء الحكيم على هذا من صفات الفعل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r7.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r7.claim: A group derives al-Ḥakīm from preventing corruption, as a bridle-bit restrains a horse from wandering without purpose.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r7.anchor: وقال قوم: «الحكيم» المانع من الفساد ومنه سميت حكمة اللجام لأنها تمنع الفرس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r8.speaker: جرير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r8.claim: Jareer supplies poetic evidence for restraining: he urges the Banū Ḥanīfa to restrain their foolish people.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r8.anchor: قال جرير: أبني حنيفة أحكموا سفهاءكم إني أخاف عليكم أن أغضبا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r9.speaker: زهير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r9.claim: Zuhayr uses أحكمت for fastening reins made of hide and hemp, supporting the sense of making firm or restraining.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r9.anchor: وقال زهير: القائد الخيل منكوبا دوابرها قد أحكمت حكمات القد والأبقا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r10.claim: The Arabs use أحكم اليتيم to mean restrain him; a well-secured sūra is protected against alteration, and wisdom restrains its possessor from ignorance.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r10.anchor: والعرب تقول: أحكم اليتيم عن كذا وكذا يريدون منعه. والسورة المحكمة: الممنوعة من التغيير

QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r11.claim: أحكم means to perfect something and keep it from departing its intended course; مُحْكَم and حَكِيم are intensive forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:32#3/r11.anchor: ويقال: أحكم الشيء إذا أتقنه ومنعه من الخروج عما يريد. فهو محكم وحكيم على التكثير

RAZI-FULL:v2p191/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p191/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p191/r1.claim: Because common usage reserves unqualified 'teacher' for someone professionally engaged in instruction, God is not called teacher without qualification; the same custom excludes schoolmasters from a bequest to learners.
RAZI-FULL:v2p191/r1.anchor: حصل في هذه اللفظة تعارف على وجه لا يجوز إطلاقه عليه وهو من يحترف بالتعليم والتلقين

RAZI-FULL:v2p191/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p191/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p191/r2.claim: Without that customary restriction, calling God the teacher would be fitting and even required, since only God can produce knowledge in another; Rāzī cites 55:2.
RAZI-FULL:v2p191/r2.anchor: لولا هذا التعارف لحسن إطلاقه عليه بل كان يجب أن لا يستعمل إلا فيه تعالى لأن المعلم هو الذي يحصل العلم في غيره

RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r1.speaker: الذين اعتقدوا أن الملائكة أتوا بالمعصية
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r1.claim: Those who hold that the angels sinned take their statement as recognizing their error in asking about humanity, repenting, and apologizing.
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r1.anchor: الذين اعتقدوا أن الملائكة أتوا بالمعصية في قولهم : { أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها } قالوا : إنهم لما عرفوا

RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r2.speaker: الذين أنكروا معصيتهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r2.claim: One explanation from those denying angelic sin is that the angels confessed inability: they could not know what God had not taught them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r2.anchor: الأول : أنهم إنما قالوا ذلك على وجه الاعتراف بالعجز والتسليم بأنهم لا يعلمون ما سئلوا عنه

RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r3.speaker: الذين أنكروا معصيتهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r3.claim: A second explanation is that God had informed the angels that humans would corrupt and kill, prompting their question, but had not taught them the names' identities.
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r3.anchor: الثاني : أن الملائكة إنما قالوا : { أتجعل فيها } لأن الله تعالى أعلمهم ذلك فكأنهم قالوا إنك أعلمتنا أنهم يفسدون

RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r4.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r4.claim: The Ashʿarites use the verse to show that God creates acquired knowledge; Rāzī argues that merely setting evidence is not teaching, because the learner's act of considering it produces knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r4.anchor: احتج أصحابنا بقوله تعالى : { لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا } على أن المعارف مخلوقة لله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r5.claim: The Muʿtazilites say knowledge comes from God through instruction or by establishing evidence; Rāzī rejects this because evidence alone does not cause knowledge without the learner's own reasoning.
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r5.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة المراد أنه لا علم لنا إلا من جهته إما بالتعليم وإما بنصب الدلالة

RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r6.speaker: أهل الإسلام
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r6.claim: Muslims infer that unseen matters are known only through God's teaching, citing 6:59 and 72:26–27.
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r6.anchor: احتج أهل الإسلام بهذه الآية على أنه لا سبيل إلى معرفة المغيبات إلا بتعليم الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r7.speaker: المنجم
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r7.claim: An astrologer can answer a Muʿtazilite that planetary motions are divinely created signs of worldly conditions, so learning from them also counts as God's instruction.
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r7.anchor: وللمنجم أن يقول للمعتزلي إذا فسرت التعليم بوضع الدلائل فعندي حركات النجوم دلائل خلقها الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r8.claim: Since even angels could not know the unseen, human beings are still less able to reach it independently.
RAZI-FULL:v2p191#2/r8.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال أيضا إن الملائكة لما عجزوا عن معرفة الغيب فلأن يعجز عنه أحدنا كان أولى

RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r1.claim: Al-ʿAlīm is an emphatic name for complete knowledge of every knowable; only God has that scope, so the unqualified name is exclusive to Him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r1.anchor: العليم من صفات المبالغة التامة في العلم ، والمبالغة التامة لا تتحقق إلا عند الإحاطة بكل المعلومات

RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r2.claim: Ḥakīm can mean all-knowing, an essential attribute eternal in the past, or one whose acts admit no objection, an attribute of action that is not eternal.
RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r2.anchor: الحكيم يستعمل على وجهين : أحدهما : بمعنى العليم فيكون ذلك من صفات الذات ، وعلى هذا التفسير نقول : إنه تعالى حكيم في الأزل

RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r3.claim: Rāzī prefers the second sense to avoid repeating 'all-knowing': the angels mean God knows all and can teach Adam, and acts wisely in this decision.
RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r3.anchor: والأقرب ههنا أن يكون المراد هو المعنى الثاني وإلا لزم التكرار ، فكأن الملائكة قالت : أنت العالم بكل المعلومات فأمكنك تعليم آدم

RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the angels meant that God is the one who decreed Adam to be a vicegerent on earth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p192/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : أن مراد الملائكة من الحكيم ، أنه هو الذي حكم بجعل آدم خليفة في الأرض
